summary.en: Select instructions for an explicit two-register machine, track descriptors, and reason about liveness, interference and spills.
summary.bn: ছোট একটি মেশিন মডেলে তুমি TAC থেকে ইনস্ট্রাকশন বাছবে এবং রেজিস্টার কম হলে spill করবে।

notes: Python programs use the standard library and were executed with Python 3.12.14.

sections.title: From local choices to function code

practice.title: Select a target sequence
practice.statementHtml: Generate and trace result=(a+b)*(c-d) on the stated two-register machine.
hints: Keep both child results until multiplication.
practice.answerHtml:
Generate result = (a+b)*(c-d). First compute the left child in R0, then the right child in R1. Multiplication can combine the two register values without a spill because neither intermediate needs to survive separately afterwards.

Complete two-register selection trace
StepInstructionR0 afterwardsR1 afterwardsRelevant memory
1LD R0, aaunusedOriginal inputs
2ADD R0, ba+bunusedOriginal inputs
3LD R1, ca+bcOriginal inputs
4SUB R1, da+bc-dOriginal inputs
5MUL R0, R1(a+b)*(c-d)c-d, now deadOriginal inputs
6ST result, R0Productdeadresult = product

With a=2, b=3, c=9 and d=5, the registers become 5 and 4 before multiplication. The stored result is 20. This concrete trace checks the chosen order, but the semantic argument is stronger: every instruction implements the corresponding child or parent operation for all allowed integer inputs.

practice.title: Track valid copies
practice.statementHtml: Track register and address descriptors for t=a+b; result=t*c when t is dead afterwards.
hints: Memory is not current until a store occurs.
practice.answerHtml:
A register descriptor records which value currently occupies a register. An address descriptor records the valid locations holding a value, including memory and registers. If a new value is computed in R0, memory for its destination may still contain an older value until a store occurs.

Descriptor changes for t=a+b; result=t*c
After instructionRegister descriptorAddress descriptor for tAddress descriptor for result
LD R0,aR0 holds anot definednot defined
ADD R0,bR0 holds t{R0}not defined
MUL R0,cR0 holds result{} if t is dead{R0}
ST result,R0R0 holds result{}{R0,memory[result]}

Descriptors describe validity, not merely the last spelling printed in code. After ADD, R0 no longer holds the old a value. Memory[a] is still valid because the operation did not assign to a. If t is live after multiplication, overwriting its only copy would be wrong and the generator must preserve it first.

practice.title: Colour live values
practice.statementHtml: Find interference edges for t1,t2,t3 with the displayed live sets and allocate two registers.
hints: Values with disjoint live ranges can share a register.
practice.answerHtml:
Two values interfere when they must be available at the same time and cannot share one physical register in the chosen representation. An interference graph uses values as vertices and simultaneous-live requirements as edges. Assigning registers resembles colouring that graph with the available register colours.

Liveness around three arithmetic temporaries
Program pointLive temporariesRequired simultaneous values
After t1=a+b{t1}t1
After t2=c+d{t1,t2}t1 and t2
After t3=t1*t2{t2,t3}t2 needed by later output; t3 needed next
After print t2{t3}t3
After print t3{}none

The interference edges are t1—t2 and t2—t3. There is no t1—t3 edge in this example because t1 dies when t3 is produced. Two colours suffice: R0 can hold t1 and then t3, while R1 holds t2. A value's textual name is not itself a reason to allocate a new register forever.

practice.title: Plan a spill
practice.statementHtml: Generate the worked two-register spill sequence for t1=a+b; t2=c+d; t3=e+f; u=t1+t2; v=u+t3.
hints: Save a live value before overwriting its only register copy.
practice.answerHtml:
Now keep three independent values live: t1=a+b; t2=c+d; t3=e+f; u=t1+t2; v=u+t3. After computing t3, all three t values are needed. Two registers cannot simultaneously retain all three without saving one value in memory or changing the calculation schedule.

Spill plan preserving all live values
StepInstructionR0 roleR1 roleSpill slot
1LD R0,a; ADD R0,bt1unusedempty
2LD R1,c; ADD R1,dt1t2empty
3ST spill1,R0t1, also savedt2t1
4LD R0,e; ADD R0,ft3t2t1
5ADD R1,spill1t3u=t2+t1t1, no longer needed
6ADD R1,R0t3, now deadv=u+t3irrelevant
7ST v,R1deadvirrelevant

A spill saves a live value to memory so its register can be reused. Reloading is unnecessary in step 5 because this teaching target allows a memory operand. On a load-store machine, an extra load would be required. Instruction-set details therefore change the cost of the same allocation decision.

The use of t2+t1 instead of t1+t2 in step 5 is valid under our mathematical integer addition model. For subtraction, that operand swap would change the result. For a target or language with additional arithmetic restrictions, the instruction selector must respect those restrictions rather than assuming all familiar rewrites apply.

quiz.prompt: What does ADD R0,b do on the stated target?
options: Replace R0 by old R0 plus memory[b]
quiz.explanation: The first register is both an input and a destructive destination.

quiz.prompt: Why can t1 and t3 share a register in the worked interference example?
options: Their live ranges do not overlap
Every temporary can share one register
quiz.explanation: t1 dies as t3 is produced, while t2 remains separately live.

quiz.prompt: When is a spill required before overwriting a register?
options: The register has a short name
Its value is live and has no other valid copy
The next instruction is a label
quiz.explanation: Saving preserves the only available copy needed by a future use.

quiz.prompt: What does an address descriptor record?
quiz.explanation: It distinguishes current copies in registers and memory from stale storage.

quiz.prompt: Why does a memory-operand ADD reduce the worked spill cost?
options: It can use the saved value without a separate reload
It changes every subtraction into addition
quiz.explanation: The target instruction form can read the spill slot directly.

quiz.prompt: What should happen to a caller-saved register's live value across a call?
options: Preserve it according to the calling convention
quiz.explanation: The callee may overwrite caller-saved registers.

quiz.prompt: What is the result for a=2,b=3,c=9,d=5 in the expression trace?
quiz.explanation: The child values are 5 and 4, whose product is 20.

quiz.prompt: Why must target side effects be included in instruction selection?
options: Flags or exceptions may affect later behaviour
quiz.explanation: A shorter sequence can be wrong if it changes observable target effects.

quiz.prompt: Which pair interferes in the worked graph?
quiz.explanation: t1 and t2 are simultaneously live after t2 is computed.

quiz.prompt: When can a dead register value be overwritten without a store?
options: When no required future use needs it
quiz.explanation: Deadness removes the need to preserve that value for later computation.

quiz.prompt: Why is one physical register per TAC name impractical?
options: The register file is finite and live ranges can be reused
Every temporary must stay in memory forever
quiz.explanation: Allocation maps many temporary lifetimes onto a limited physical register set.

keyPoints.en: Instruction selection depends on the stated target machine.
keyPoints.bn: কোন ইনস্ট্রাকশন নেওয়া যাবে, তা টার্গেট মেশিন দেখে ঠিক করো।

keyPoints.en: Descriptors must track valid value copies after each overwrite.
keyPoints.bn: রেজিস্টার বদলালে কোন কপি এখনো ঠিক আছে, তা আপডেট করো।

keyPoints.en: Values with overlapping live ranges may need different registers.
keyPoints.bn: একই সময়ে দরকারি মানগুলোকে আলাদা রেজিস্টার লাগতে পারে।

keyPoints.en: Spilling preserves a live value in memory before register reuse.
keyPoints.bn: রেজিস্টার আবার ব্যবহারের আগে দরকারি মান মেমরিতে spill করো।

keyPoints.en: Calling conventions constrain values that survive a call.
keyPoints.bn: ফাংশন কলের পর মান রাখতে calling convention-এর নিয়ম মানো।
